title: Undo uncommitted sample changes
summary: A savepoint marks a point inside a transaction.
introduction: A savepoint marks a point inside a transaction. Your task: Explain which insert the savepoint rollback undoes.
learningObjectives: Explain which insert the savepoint rollback undoes.
Explain the example for undo uncommitted sample changes

blocks.text: A savepoint marks a point inside a transaction. ROLLBACK TO can undo later changes while keeping earlier work in that transaction.
Use Oracle Database 19c+ with a SQL editor in a new practice schema. Oracle SQL and PL/SQL do not run in this site's SQLite playground. Create only the named sample objects in that practice schema.

blocks.title: Undo uncommitted sample changes

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `ROLLBACK` cancels the applicable uncommitted changes. It cannot undo an earlier committed transaction.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.
`WHERE` keeps only rows that pass its condition. Check the condition with sample data before using it for a change.

blocks.text: The extra sample title is not returned after the rollback to the savepoint.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: This demonstration assumes no earlier row has that title. Do not run DDL between the savepoint and rollback.
